stances_toward.note: Part of the Realm with self-government since 2009; Copenhagen keeps foreign and defence policy and pays the block grant, but the Self-Government Act (section 21) gives the people of Greenland the right to decide on independence, subject to a referendum and Folketing consent. Nuuk's government (Nielsen, Demokraatit, since March 2025) opposes joining the US but is also a negotiating party: the Danish line is that Greenland's red line is Denmark's. Own territory, but not a territory Denmark can dispose of alone. Bond - kin: the Realm, with a colonial history that the 2025-26 crisis has reopened.

relations_to.summary: Denmark holds and defends sovereignty and territorial integrity over Greenland as part of the Realm; the third Frederiksen government's programme (June 2026) pledges to uphold both and to involve Greenland's government fully in foreign-policy decisions touching the island. Greenland's prime minister Nielsen says Greenland does not want to be owned or governed by the US (January 2026).

relations_to.summary: Greenland is a self-governing part of the Realm under the 2009 Self-Government Act, whose section 21 gives the people of Greenland the right to decide on independence (negotiated agreement, Greenland referendum, consent of Inatsisartut and the Folketing).

relations_to.summary: Denmark pays Greenland an annual block grant of about USD 623m (roughly USD 11,000 a head, by one estimate), nearer USD 1bn a year counting other services, and a further DKK 1.6bn pledged for health and infrastructure to 2029. It is Copenhagen's main economic argument against American money offers.

relations_to.summary: Arctic build-up for Greenland - DKK 14.6bn (27 Jan 2025: ships, drones, radar, Joint Arctic Command) and DKK 27.4bn (10 Oct 2025: Arctic special-forces unit, East Greenland radar, new undersea cable, two Arctic vessels), plus the January 2026 reinforcement (Operation Arctic Endurance) with French, Swedish, Norwegian and German contingents.

relations_to.summary: Greenland's election of 11 Mar 2025 returned Demokraatit (29.9%, gradual independence, Nielsen premier in a broad coalition with three-quarters of the seats) ahead of Naleraq (24.5%, fast independence, closer US ties) and Inuit Ataqatigiit (21.4%); the Kingdom holds the Arctic Council chair for 2025-2027 with Greenland leading it, a first.
